prompt: A researcher studying a trading desk concludes she can't say where the trader ends and the screens, feeds and order system begin: 'trading' only exists as all of them performed together.
tells: 'trading' only exists as all of them performed together
why: The social and material are inseparable in the practice itself.
trap: Imbrication keeps human and material agencies distinct; here they can't be pulled apart.

prompt: A study of a search engine finds the ranking isn't a tool people use; it is made, moment to moment, by code, users' clicks and engineers' tweaks, none of which exists apart.
why: The practice is sociomaterial through and through.
trap: No model is reshaping the world it describes; the claim is inseparability.

prompt: An ethnographer of consultants finds 'being available' is not a habit plus a device but one practice: the phone, the buzzing, the quick replies and client expectations performed as one.
tells: not a habit plus a device but one practice
why: Habit and device are constituted together.
trap: Affordance would treat the phone and the user as separate things that meet.

prompt: In robotic surgery, a study finds the surgeon's skill can't be described without the robot, the console and the team's talk; skill itself is the sociomaterial assemblage at work.
tells: skill itself is the sociomaterial assemblage at work
why: Skill is performed by the inseparable mix.

prompt: At an emergency dispatch center, researchers find 'the emergency' isn't the caller's words plus the software: it is produced by the on-screen questions, the map and the dispatcher's voice together, inseparably.
tells: produced by the on-screen questions, the map and the dispatcher's voice together, inseparably
why: People and tech can't be separated in the practice.
trap: Not two subsystems in balance; one inseparable practice.

prompt: In a warehouse with wrist scanners, researchers find there is no 'worker' and 'device' to compare: the pace, the beeps and the picker's body make up one performance of picking.
tells: there is no 'worker' and 'device' to compare
why: The practice is one inseparable mix.
trap: It's not the scanner causing the pace.
